```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Schalkwijk_2018_efavirenz"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Schalkwijk_2018_efavirenz"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-018-0642-9> (open access, PMC6182466)

Schalkwijk et al. built a mechanism-based population PK model of efavirenz in
pregnant and non-pregnant women, then simulated 400 mg and 600 mg once daily in
the third trimester to ask whether the reduced dose is adequate in pregnancy.
Pregnancy acts through three routes in the model:

1. falling serum albumin over gestation raises the unbound fraction `fu`
   (Eqs 4-5), which raises the apparent hepatic clearance of a low-extraction
   drug;
2. falling haematocrit raises hepatic plasma flow (Eqs 3, 6);
3. a dichotomous pregnancy effect shortens the mean absorption time and raises
   relative bioavailability by 16% (Table 2).

CYP2B6 metabolizer phenotype selects one of three intrinsic clearances.

# Population

The model was developed on 1749 plasma samples from 247 women with HIV pooled
from six studies (Studies 2-7 of Table 1). Study 1 (11 women, 219 samples) was
held out for external evaluation; including it gives the 258 women and 1968
samples (774 during pregnancy) quoted in the Abstract. 142 women contributed
samples both during pregnancy (second or third trimester; gestational age 21-39
weeks) and postpartum, and 116 only when not pregnant. Median body weight ranged
from 53 to 83 kg across studies. Women were Black, Caucasian, Thai and Hispanic
across the studies (Table 1). All but five women took efavirenz 600 mg once
daily. CYP2B6 genotype was available only for Study 7 (18% of women: 10 poor,
25 intermediate, 26 extensive metabolizers).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Schalkwijk_2018_efavirenz")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. Eqs 1-9
are not legible in the PDF text layer; they were read from the MathML of the
EuropePMC full-text XML of the same article.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lmtt` (MAT, non-pregnant) | log(2.12 h) | Table 2 |
| `lmtt_preg` (MAT, pregnant) | log(1.67 h) | Table 2 |
| `lfdepot` | fixed log(1) | Methods 2.3 |
| `e_preg_fdepot` | 0.16 | Table 2, 'F (%) relative to non-pregnant women' = 116 |
| `lclint` (EM) | log(4580 L/h) | Table 2 |
| `lclint_im` | log(3340 L/h) | Table 2 |
| `lclint_pm` | log(1380 L/h) | Table 2 |
| `lvc` | log(133 L) | Table 2 |
| `lvp` | log(390 L) | Table 2 |
| `lq` | log(35 L/h) | Table 2 |
| `lqh` (Qhep) | fixed log(109 L/h) | Methods 2.2 |
| `lkd` (kD) | fixed log(2.05 uM) | Methods 2.2 |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | fixed 0.75, 1 | Methods 2.3 (70 kg reference) |
| `etalclint` | 0.0975 (32% CV) | Table 2 |
| `etalmtt` | 0.177 (44% CV) | Table 2 |
| `etaiov_lfdepot_1..6` | 0.0560 (24% CV) | Table 2; Methods 2.3 (1-6 visits) |
| `propSd` | 0.18 | Table 2 |
| Mixture frequencies PM / IM / EM | 14 / 36 / 50% (fixed) | Results paragraph 2 |
| `CLhep/F = Qhep,plasma * Eh` | n/a | Eq 1 |
| `Eh = CLint * fu / (Qhep,plasma + CLint * fu)` | n/a | Eq 2 |
| `Qhep,plasma = (1 - Ht) * Qhep` | n/a | Eq 3 |
| `fu = kD / (kD + [P])` | n/a | Eq 4 |
| `[P] (uM) = (45.8 - 0.1775 GA - 0.0033 GA^2) / 0.07` | n/a | Eq 5 |
| `Ht (%) = 39.1 - 0.0544 GA - 0.0021 GA^2` | n/a | Eq 6 |
| `ktr = (n + 1) / MAT`, n = 3 | n/a | Eq 7; Fig 1 caption |
| `Cfree = fu * Ctot` (model output `Cu`) | n/a | Eq 9 |

# Virtual cohort

Methods 2.7 describes the simulation cohort behind Table 3: body weight
log-normal with geometric mean 62 kg (geometric SD 1.3), gestational age normal
with mean 34 and SD 2.3 weeks for the third trimester, and 400 or 600 mg once
daily to steady state, stratified by CYP2B6 phenotype. The paper used 500
subjects per phenotype; this vignette uses 150 per arm (12 arms).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20180308)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20180308)

n_per_arm <- 150
arms <- expand.grid(
  phenotype = c("PM", "IM", "EM"),
  dose_mg = c(600, 400),
  preg_state = c("Non-pregnant", "Pregnant"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
arms$arm_id <- seq_len(nrow(arms))

obs_times <- 696 + c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24)

make_arm <- function(a, n) {
  ids <- (a$arm_id - 1L) * n + seq_len(n)
  subj <- tibble(
    id = ids,
    WT = exp(rnorm(n, log(62), log(1.3))),
    PREG = as.integer(a$preg_state == "Pregnant"),
    EGA = if (a$preg_state == "Pregnant") rnorm(n, 34, 2.3) else 0,
    CYP2B6_PM = as.integer(a$phenotype == "PM"),
    CYP2B6_IM = as.integer(a$phenotype == "IM"),
    OCC = 1L,
    phenotype = a$phenotype,
    preg_state = a$preg_state,
    dose_mg = a$dose_mg,
    arm = paste(a$preg_state, paste(a$dose_mg, "mg"), a$phenotype, sep = " | ")
  )
  doses <- subj |>
    mutate(time = 0, amt = a$dose_mg, ii = 24, addl = 29, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, ii = 0, addl = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs)
}

events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) make_arm(arms[i, ], n_per_arm))) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Schalkwijk_2018_efavirenz")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("arm", "phenotype", "preg_state", "dose_mg")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Typical-value check against Table 3

Table 3 reports cohort medians. For a log-normal clearance the median AUC24 is
close to the typical-value AUC24, so a deterministic solve at the cohort's
typical covariates (62 kg, 34 weeks of gestation) is a sharp test of the
structural model and of every value in Table 2.

```{r typical}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

typ_events <- arms |>
  mutate(
    id = arm_id,
    WT = 62,
    PREG = as.integer(preg_state == "Pregnant"),
    EGA = 34 * PREG,
    CYP2B6_PM = as.integer(phenotype == "PM"),
    CYP2B6_IM = as.integer(phenotype == "IM"),
    OCC = 1L
  )
typ_events <- bind_rows(
  typ_events |> mutate(time = 0, amt = dose_mg, ii = 24, addl = 29, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  typ_events |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = seq(696, 720, by = 0.1)) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, ii = 0, addl = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = typ_events, keep = c("phenotype", "preg_state", "dose_mg")) |>
  as.data.frame()

trap <- function(x, y) sum(diff(x) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
typ_sum <- typ |>
  group_by(id, phenotype, preg_state, dose_mg) |>
  summarise(
    auc24 = trap(time, Cc),
    c12 = Cc[which.min(abs(time - 708))],
    auc24_free = trap(time, Cu),
    c12_free = Cu[which.min(abs(time - 708))],
    .groups = "drop"
  )

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~preg_state, ~dose_mg, ~phenotype, ~auc24_pub, ~c12_pub,
  "Non-pregnant", 600, "PM", 154, 6.1,
  "Non-pregnant", 600, "IM", 63, 2.4,
  "Non-pregnant", 600, "EM", 46, 1.7,
  "Non-pregnant", 400, "PM", 103, 4.1,
  "Non-pregnant", 400, "IM", 42, 1.6,
  "Non-pregnant", 400, "EM", 31, 1.1,
  "Pregnant", 600, "PM", 140, 5.4,
  "Pregnant", 600, "IM", 57, 2.1,
  "Pregnant", 600, "EM", 42, 1.4,
  "Pregnant", 400, "PM", 93, 3.9,
  "Pregnant", 400, "IM", 38, 1.4,
  "Pregnant", 400, "EM", 28, 1.0
)

typ_cmp <- typ_sum |>
  inner_join(published, by = c("preg_state", "dose_mg", "phenotype")) |>
  mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (auc24 - auc24_pub) / auc24_pub,
    c12_pct = 100 * (c12 - c12_pub) / c12_pub
  ) |>
  arrange(preg_state, desc(dose_mg), factor(phenotype, levels = c("PM", "IM", "EM")))

typ_cmp |>
  transmute(
    preg_state, dose_mg, phenotype,
    auc24 = round(auc24, 1), auc24_pub, auc_pct = round(auc_pct, 1),
    c12 = round(c12, 2), c12_pub, c12_pct = round(c12_pct, 1)
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Pregnancy state" = preg_state,
    "Dose (mg QD)" = dose_mg,
    "Phenotype" = phenotype,
    "AUC24 typical (mg*h/L)" = auc24,
    "AUC24 Table 3" = auc24_pub,
    "AUC24 % diff" = auc_pct,
    "C12 typical (mg/L)" = c12,
    "C12 Table 3" = c12_pub,
    "C12 % diff" = c12_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value steady-state AUC24 and C12 (62 kg; 34 weeks gestation) vs Table 3 medians.")
```

All twelve AUC24 values agree with Table 3 to within 2%. Eleven of twelve C12
values agree to within the rounding of the published one- or two-digit values.
The exception is the poor-metabolizer, pregnant, 400 mg cell: Table 3 prints a
C12 of 3.9 mg/L with an IQR of 2.7-4.7, while its own AUC24 (93 mg*h/L) is
exactly two-thirds of the 600 mg cell (140), whose C12 is 5.4. Linear PK gives
5.4 x 2/3 = 3.6, which the model reproduces; the printed 3.9 sits off-centre in
its own IQR and is treated as a typesetting slip (see Assumptions and
deviations).

```{r typical-gate}
# Deterministic solve, so tight bounds are appropriate. A mis-transcribed
# CLint, volume, Qhep, kD or polynomial coefficient moves AUC24 by >5%.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(typ_cmp$auc_pct) < 3),
  all(abs(typ_cmp$c12_pct[!(typ_cmp$preg_state == "Pregnant" & typ_cmp$dose_mg == 400 &
    typ_cmp$phenotype == "PM")]) < 7)
)
```

## Pregnancy ratios quoted in the Abstract and Results

```{r ratios}
ratio_tab <- typ_sum |>
  filter(dose_mg == 400) |>
  select(phenotype, preg_state, auc24, c12, auc24_free, c12_free) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = preg_state, values_from = c(auc24, c12, auc24_free, c12_free)) |>
  transmute(
    phenotype,
    auc_total = `auc24_Pregnant` / `auc24_Non-pregnant`,
    c12_total = `c12_Pregnant` / `c12_Non-pregnant`,
    auc_free = `auc24_free_Pregnant` / `auc24_free_Non-pregnant`,
    c12_free = `c12_free_Pregnant` / `c12_free_Non-pregnant`
  )

ratio_tab |>
  mutate(across(-phenotype, \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    "Phenotype" = phenotype,
    "Total AUC24 (paper 0.91)" = auc_total,
    "Total C12 (paper 0.87)" = c12_total,
    "Free AUC24 (paper 1.15)" = auc_free,
    "Free C12 (paper 1.11)" = c12_free
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Pregnant / non-pregnant ratios, typical subject, 400 mg QD.")

fu_np <- mod_typ |>
  rxode2::rxSolve(events = typ_events |> filter(id == 1, evid == 0) |> slice(1)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  pull(fu)

stopifnot(
  all(abs(ratio_tab$auc_total - 0.91) < 0.02),
  all(abs(ratio_tab$c12_total - 0.87) < 0.03),
  all(abs(ratio_tab$auc_free - 1.15) < 0.03),
  all(abs(ratio_tab$c12_free - 1.11) < 0.04),
  # Methods 2.7: 0.7 mg/L x non-pregnant fu = 0.002 mg/L free target
  abs(0.7 * fu_np - 0.002) < 0.0003
)
```

The model reproduces the Abstract's 91% (total AUC24) and 87% (total C12)
pregnant-to-non-pregnant ratios, and the Results' 15% (free AUC24) and 11%
(free C12) increases. The non-pregnant unbound fraction is
`r signif(fu_np, 3)`, so the 0.7 mg/L total target maps to the paper's free
target of 0.002 mg/L.

## Unbound fraction over gestation (ESM 2 figure)

```{r fu-ga}
fu_ga <- tibble(EGA = seq(0, 40, by = 0.5)) |>
  mutate(
    alb = (45.8 - 0.1775 * EGA - 0.0033 * EGA^2) / 0.07,
    fu = 2.05 / (2.05 + alb)
  )
ggplot(fu_ga, aes(EGA, 100 * fu)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Gestational age (weeks)", y = "Efavirenz unbound fraction (%)",
    caption = "Replicates the fu-vs-gestational-age figure of Schalkwijk 2018 ESM 2 (Eqs 4-5)."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation against Table 3

The stochastic cohort includes IIV on CLint/F and MAT and inter-occasion
variability on F (one occasion per subject).

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  distinct(id, arm, amt) |>
  mutate(time = 696)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id, doseu = "mg")

intervals <- data.frame(start = 696, end = 720, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

ref_nca <- published |>
  transmute(
    arm = paste(preg_state, paste(dose_mg, "mg"), phenotype, sep = " | "),
    auclast = auc24_pub
  )

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = ref_nca,
  by = "arm",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated median steady-state AUC24 (PKNCA) vs Table 3 medians. * differs by >20%.")
```

```{r pknca-gate}
sim_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(auc_med = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(ref_nca, by = "arm") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (auc_med - auclast) / auclast)

# Each cell is a median of 150 subjects with ~40% CV on AUC24, so its
# sampling SE is ~4%; the median over 12 cells has an SE of ~1.6%. One
# 16-thread render gave a median of -3.5% and a worst cell of -7.7%, all
# sampling noise (the analytic F * Dose / (fu * CLint) medians of the same
# subjects agree with PKNCA). The deterministic typical-value gate above
# carries the tight structural check.
stopifnot(
  nrow(sim_auc) == 12,
  abs(median(sim_auc$pct)) < 7,
  max(abs(sim_auc$pct)) < 15
)
```

## Mid-dose concentrations and target attainment

```{r c12}
c12_sim <- sim |>
  filter(time == 708) |>
  group_by(preg_state, dose_mg, phenotype) |>
  summarise(
    c12_med = median(Cc),
    below_1 = 100 * mean(Cc < 1),
    below_07 = 100 * mean(Cc < 0.7),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pct_published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~preg_state, ~dose_mg, ~phenotype, ~below_1_pub, ~below_07_pub,
  "Non-pregnant", 600, "PM", 0, 0,
  "Non-pregnant", 600, "IM", 3, 0,
  "Non-pregnant", 600, "EM", 9, 2,
  "Non-pregnant", 400, "PM", 0, 0,
  "Non-pregnant", 400, "IM", 15, 4,
  "Non-pregnant", 400, "EM", 41, 14,
  "Pregnant", 600, "PM", 0, 0,
  "Pregnant", 600, "IM", 7, 1,
  "Pregnant", 600, "EM", 23, 5,
  "Pregnant", 400, "PM", 0, 0,
  "Pregnant", 400, "IM", 23, 8,
  "Pregnant", 400, "EM", 53, 26
)

c12_tab <- c12_sim |>
  inner_join(published, by = c("preg_state", "dose_mg", "phenotype")) |>
  inner_join(pct_published, by = c("preg_state", "dose_mg", "phenotype")) |>
  arrange(preg_state, desc(dose_mg), factor(phenotype, levels = c("PM", "IM", "EM")))

c12_tab |>
  transmute(
    preg_state, dose_mg, phenotype,
    c12_med = round(c12_med, 2), c12_pub,
    below_1 = round(below_1), below_1_pub,
    below_07 = round(below_07), below_07_pub
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Pregnancy state" = preg_state,
    "Dose (mg QD)" = dose_mg,
    "Phenotype" = phenotype,
    "C12 median (mg/L)" = c12_med,
    "C12 Table 3" = c12_pub,
    "% < 1 mg/L" = below_1,
    "% < 1 mg/L Table 3" = below_1_pub,
    "% < 0.7 mg/L" = below_07,
    "% < 0.7 mg/L Table 3" = below_07_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated C12 and target attainment vs Table 3.")

# The extensive-metabolizer 400 mg cells carry the paper's dose_mg-reduction
# argument (41% non-pregnant, 53% pregnant below 1 mg/L). A binomial
# proportion near 50% from 150 subjects has SE ~4 points.
em400 <- c12_tab |> filter(dose_mg == 400, phenotype == "EM")
stopifnot(all(abs(em400$below_1 - em400$below_1_pub) < 15))
```

## Figure 4: total and free C12 at 400 mg

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim |>
  filter(time == 708, dose_mg == 400) |>
  select(id, preg_state, phenotype, Total = Cc, Free = Cu) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Total, Free), names_to = "measure", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(
    phenotype = factor(phenotype, levels = c("PM", "IM", "EM")),
    measure = factor(measure, levels = c("Total", "Free"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(phenotype, conc, fill = preg_state)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(
    data = tibble(measure = factor(c("Total", "Free"), levels = c("Total", "Free")), target = c(0.7, 0.002)),
    aes(yintercept = target), linetype = "dotted"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "CYP2B6 phenotype", y = "C12 (mg/L)", fill = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Schalkwijk 2018: efavirenz 400 mg QD, third trimester vs non-pregnant."
  )
```

```{r profile, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim |>
  filter(dose_mg == 400) |>
  mutate(tad = time - 696, phenotype = factor(phenotype, levels = c("PM", "IM", "EM"))) |>
  group_by(tad, preg_state, phenotype) |>

  labs(

```

The paper's Fig. 3 (prediction-corrected VPC against the observed data) cannot
be reproduced without the individual data.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Algebraic well-stirred liver.** Fig. 1 draws a physical liver compartment
  with volume `Vh`, but `Vh` is not reported in the paper or either supplement.
  The maintainers encoded the liver as the paper's own algebraic Eqs 1-2:
  systemic clearance `Qhep,plasma * Eh` from the central compartment, and a
  first-pass loss of the fraction `Eh` on drug leaving the last transit
  compartment. Steady-state AUC does not depend on `Vh`, and this encoding
  reproduces all twelve Table 3 AUC24 medians to within 2%. Both the first-pass
  factor and the allometric scaling of `Qhep` are needed; dropping either moves
  the predictions 10-20% from Table 3.
- **Allometric scaling of Qhep.** Methods 2.3 scales "all flow parameters" to
  70 kg with exponent 0.75. The maintainers applied this to the literature
  hepatic blood flow `Qhep` (109 L/h) as well as to CLint/F and Q/F; the
  Table 3 reproduction confirms it.
- **Mixture model encoded as covariates.** The paper estimated CYP2B6
  phenotype as a three-subpopulation mixture on CLint/F with frequencies fixed
  to 14 / 36 / 50% (PM / IM / EM). The model file takes the phenotype as the
  indicator columns `CYP2B6_PM` and `CYP2B6_IM` (extensive metabolizer when
  both are 0). To simulate an unphenotyped population, draw the indicators with
  the paper's 14 / 36 / 50% frequencies.
- **Pooled poor-metabolizer level.** The paper's poor-metabolizer subpopulation
  combines the 'slow' (516TT, or 516GT with 983TC) and 'very slow' (983CC)
  genotype classes listed in Methods 2.2. The maintainers ratified the new
  canonical covariate `CYP2B6_PM` for this pooled level rather than reusing the
  strict `CYP2B6_SM`, whose 983CC subjects would otherwise fall to the
  extensive-metabolizer clearance. The four-class sentence in Methods 2.2 lists
  983CC under both 'slow' and 'very slow'; the three-level grouping actually
  fitted is unambiguous and is what is encoded.
- **Two pregnancy covariates.** Gestational age (`EGA`, weeks; 0 when not
  pregnant) drives the albumin and haematocrit polynomials; the binary `PREG`
  carries the MAT and F effects. Supply `PREG = 1` exactly when `EGA > 0`.
  Table 1 labels gestational age in "years"; the values and Methods 2.7 show
  the unit is weeks.
- **Inter-occasion variability.** IOV on F is encoded with six occasion slots
  (Methods 2.3: one to six assessment visits per woman), all sharing the
  estimated variance. This vignette sets `OCC = 1` for every subject.
- **%CV to variance.** IIV and IOV were reported as %CV and converted with
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`.
- **C12 for poor metabolizers, pregnant, 400 mg.** Table 3 prints 3.9 mg/L
  (IQR 2.7-4.7). Under the linear PK the paper assumes, this cell should be
  two-thirds of the 600 mg cell (5.4 mg/L), i.e. about 3.6 mg/L, as the
  printed AUC24 values are (93 vs 140). The model gives about 3.6 mg/L; the
  cell is excluded from the C12 gate.
- **Simulation size.** The paper simulated 500 women per phenotype; this
  vignette uses 150 per arm, so the stochastic medians and target-attainment
  percentages carry a few percentage points of sampling noise.
- No erratum to the article was found (checked 2026-10-16).
